change: Fix links on your site that lead nowhere
signal: A link points to a page that no longer exists
why: A dead link sends a customer to an error page and wastes the visit. Fixing it is mechanical — there is no wording involved, so there is nothing for you to have an opinion about.

change: Keep the page list you give Google accurate
signal: The list includes a page that has moved or been removed
why: Google treats a list full of missing pages as a sign the site is poorly kept, and trusts the rest of it less. Keeping it tidy costs nothing and is impossible to get wrong.

change: Stop pictures making the page jump about as it loads
signal: The page shifts while loading, or a picture is far larger than it needs to be
why: When a picture loads late, everything below it jumps down and people tap the wrong thing. Telling the page how big the picture will be prevents it, and cannot change what the page says.

change: Keep pages inside a set weight limit so they stay fast
signal: A page grows heavier than its limit, or starts loading more slowly for real visitors
why: Google publishes the speeds a page has to hit: the main content within 2.5 seconds, a response to a tap within 0.2 seconds, and no jumping about. A weight limit keeps you inside them automatically.

change: Repair broken labels that describe your pages
signal: A label is malformed, or is missing something it needs to work
why: Every page carries hidden labels telling search engines what it is — a service, a question, a business. A broken label is ignored completely, so it looks present while doing nothing at all.

change: Add a new type of label to a page
signal: A page's content fits a description it does not yet claim
why: A label is a claim about what the page is, and claiming the wrong thing damages trust with search engines. We add it, then email you the same day with the page and the claim written out in plain English, so a wrong one is one reply away from being removed.

change: Link related pages to each other
signal: Two pages cover related things but nothing joins them, or a page is buried too deep
why: Links help people find the next thing they need, and help search engines see how your site fits together. We cap how many are added so the writing never turns into a list of links.

change: Rewrite the headline and summary Google displays
signal: Lots of people see your listing in Google but few of them click it
why: This is the sentence that decides whether someone visits you or a competitor, and it is your voice, not ours. We write the new version, publish it, and email you both versions the same day with the numbers behind the change — one click puts the old one back.

change: Add a short, direct answer near the top of a page
signal: People search a question you get shown for, but no part of the page answers it plainly
why: AI assistants quote a paragraph, not a whole page. A short passage that answers one question completely is the piece they lift, and the piece a hurried reader wants too. We add it and send you the exact wording the same day.

change: Answer the real questions people are already searching
signal: The same question keeps appearing in your search data with no answer on the site
why: The questions your customers actually type beat any keyword tool, because they are evidence rather than guesswork. We write the answer, publish it, and email it to you the same day so you can correct anything that is not quite how you would put it.

signal: Clear demand exists for something your site does not cover
why: Churning out pages to chase traffic is what Google penalises sites for, so the bar is evidence: a question people already ask in search, repeatedly, that your site does not answer. When it is met we write the page and email it to you the same day.

change: Test buttons, layout and how hard the form is to fill in
signal: People arrive, look around, and leave without getting in touch
why: Ranking higher is worth nothing if the page does not get you the enquiry. These run as proper tests against a comparison group left alone, so you find out whether it worked rather than being told. You get the result, not a request.

change: Your prices, promises, legal wording and claims about your business
why: Nothing automatic should ever be able to change what you charge or what you promise a customer. These are locked, and an attempt to edit them stops the change from going live at all.

change: The settings that control whether Google shows your site
why: One wrong setting here can remove your entire website from Google, and you would not notice for weeks. That is far too much damage for anything automatic to be trusted with.
